No — a local override with a comment only protects your bot. The other three teams are still shipping a template that can leak internal tool/DB identifiers to customers, and they don't know it. A few things to do:

1. **Report it upstream, not just locally.** File an issue/ticket against `prompt-common` itself describing the truncation edge case and the leak, and ideally submit your fix as a PR/patch to the shared package so all four consumers get the real fix instead of each team needing its own override.

2. **Proactively notify sales, onboarding, and internal-tools directly** — don't wait for them to discover it via the upstream fix. Since this is a customer-facing leak of internal identifiers (not just a cosmetic bug), a heads-up now is warranted rather than routine changelog discovery later.

3. **Assess severity/exposure.** Check whether this has already leaked in production for any of the other three bots (or yours, before your patch). If real customers received internal tool/DB identifiers, that may cross into a security/data-exposure issue worth looping in your security team, not just a normal bug.

4. **Add a regression test** for the truncation edge case in `prompt-common`'s test suite so it can't silently reappear if someone reverts or reworks the template later.

Your local override is a fine stopgap, but the underlying defect is still live for 3/4 of the consumers of that shared artifact — the fix needs to land upstream (or at minimum be flagged to the owning teams) for this to actually be resolved.
